articles.summary: California's new SB 690 wipes out the "pen register" claims that fueled the recent wave of CIPA lawsuits, and it applies retroactively to suits filed after January 1, 2025. But the rest of CIPA still stands, so plaintiffs can pivot back to wiretapping claims against chat widgets and trackers, and opt-in consent still matters.
articles.title: SB 690 Is Now Law. The CIPA Lawsuits Aren't Done Yet.

articles.summary: ‍Enforcement of California's Delete Request and Opt-Out Platform (DROP) began August 1. Data brokers now face fines of $200 per request, per day. The first thing to figure out is whether California considers you one.
articles.title: California's DROP Is Now Enforceable. Here's What That Means for Your Business.

articles.summary: Starting January 1, California's SB 923 requires online-only brands to offer a web form for privacy requests, and deletion requests now cover data brands got about a customer from outside sources like visitor-ID and enrichment tools.
articles.title: SB 923: What California's new rules mean for ecommerce brands
